# Precision matrix

<!-- Generated by tools/precision_matrix.py from docs/precision.json and docs/precision_review.yml. Edit those, not this file. -->

The test suite proves each rule **fires** on the attack it claims. This matrix proves the other half: every rule runs, unchanged, against **every** recorded capture in the repository, and must stay silent on attacks it does not claim, unless the capture genuinely contains its behaviour. A rule that returned every event would fill this page with ❌.

Last run: **2026-11-24 11:02 UTC** on Kustainer (Azure Data Explorer emulator). 12 detections × 19 captures = 228 runs.

| Result | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| · silent | 164 | ran on another technique's capture and returned nothing |
| 🎯 true positive | 0 | fired on another capture that genuinely contains the behaviour (reviewed, reason below) |
| ❌ false positive | 0 | fired where it should not: a rule bug, tracked below |
| 🔍 to review | 1 | fired on another capture, not yet classified |
| – no data | 40 | the capture has none of the tables the rule reads; proves nothing either way |
| ✅ own capture | 23 | the capture the rule's own tests use (see the README coverage table) |

**Cross-capture precision: 164 of 165 runs with data were silent or genuine hits (1 still to review).**

## Limits

- Captures are attack recordings, not a day of normal enterprise activity. Silence here proves the rule does not fire on *other attacks' surrounding activity*; precision on a real estate is proven in a tenant, in hunt or triage mode first (see [lifecycle](lifecycle.md)).
- Fixtures were converted to the tables each rule reads, so some captures are partial. Cells marked – are excluded from the precision figure rather than counted as silent.
